newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open stronger on Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open stronger on Greenspan comments.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger on Friday after comments from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan were interpreted as bullish for markets and helped spur buying from accounts, dealers said.

"Greenspan's comments last night are the catalyst that's got this thing just turned around," said a dealer with one bank-owned brokerage. "With the speech last night (he) has certainly hinted to the market, strongly hinted to the market, that rates are probably not going to go up in May."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.04 percent from 3.11 percent at Thursday's close.
Greenspan said in a speech on Thursday he expects economic growth to slow later this year and into next, but added that the central bank would need to act if that does not prove to be the case.
"It's attracting a few more buyers in this morning," the dealer said. He said the market has moved from trading in a defensive manner to buying the market on weakness.

In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.42 percent from 3.51 percent at the close of trading on Thursday. The one-year T-bill softened to yield 3.96 percent from 4.10 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, in the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
